checked: src/CLI/Sync.jl (render, slots, plan, managed_header, fragments, insert_fragments)

findings.title: README.md's Slots column claims commit-message.tmpl and bump-message.tmpl take {{package.name}}, but neither template contains that placeholder
findings.description: templates/README.md's doc-table Slots column is meant to name exactly the `{{key}}` placeholders each template contains. Grepping both templates for `{{[a-z0-9_.-]+}}` (the exact syntax `Sync.render`'s regex accepts) finds no `{{package.name}}` in either file, confirmed against the call sites (Init.jl:312 merges `s` with only `Dict("files"=>...)`; Bump.jl:35 merges `Sync.slots(cfg2)` with `from`/`to`/`files`/`abandoned`). The README overstates what these two templates consume.
findings.resolution_hint: Drop `{{package.name}}` from the Slots cell of the commit-message.tmpl and bump-message.tmpl rows in templates/README.md.

findings.title: regressions-README.md's baked-in managed header omits the version stamp every sibling embedded-header template carries
locations: templates/regressions-README.md:1 — "<!-- gbg:managed regressions-README.md — rewritten by `gbg sync`; do not edit -->"
templates/SKILL.md.tmpl:6 — "<!-- gbg:managed SKILL.md.tmpl v{{tool.version}} — rewritten by `gbg sync`; do not edit -->"
findings.description: regressions-README.md and SKILL.md.tmpl are both G-classed Markdown templates rendered identically in Sync.plan (`render(template(name), s)`), and both bake their own `<!-- gbg:managed ... -->` header into the body rather than via `Sync.managed_header`. SKILL.md.tmpl's header includes `v{{tool.version}}`, matching every other managed header format in the tool (policy files via `managed_header(:html,...)` at Sync.jl:151-152, and the CLAUDE.md/.gitignore block markers). regressions-README.md's header has no version token, so a reader of the raw file cannot tell which tool version rendered it — the one thing every other managed header exists to carry (ARCHITECTURE §0 R2 transparency). Nothing documents this as a deliberate exception.
findings.resolution_hint: Add `v{{tool.version}}` to templates/regressions-README.md:1's header line, matching SKILL.md.tmpl's form, or document it as a deliberate fleet-invariant exception in README.md's Managed headers section.

findings.title: README.md's blanket "Managed headers" rule is contradicted by queue-guard.sh.tmpl, a G, #-comment-format file that carries no gbg:managed header at all
locations: templates/README.md:26-27 — "A G file carries a first-line header where its format allows a comment: `# gbg:managed <template> v<version> — rewritten by `gbg sync`; do not edit` (`#`-commented formats)"
templates/queue-guard.sh.tmpl:1-40 (no `gbg:managed` string anywhere in the file)
src/CLI/Sync.jl:207 — `template("queue-guard.sh.tmpl")` used raw, no `render()`, no `managed_header` call
findings.description: queue-guard.sh.tmpl is listed as class G in the same README table (templates/README.md:13) and is a `#`-comment-capable shell script, so the general header rule two paragraphs later should apply per the README's own wording. In fact it is copied byte-for-byte with no header stamped at all — `managed_header`'s `:hash` branch (Sync.jl:151) is never invoked anywhere in the codebase, so no `#`-format managed file actually gets that header via that path. The README's general claim is false for at least one file it itself classifies as G; the file's own row ("none — PF's Stop hook verbatim") only explains the missing slots, not the missing header.
findings.resolution_hint: Qualify the Managed headers paragraph with the queue-guard.sh.tmpl exception (verbatim files carry no header, to keep the upstream text unmodified), or remove the dead `:hash` branch of `managed_header` and note that no shell/#-format G file currently uses a stamped header.
